caption: Acts twice applies Psalm 16 to Jesus’s resurrection and contrasts him with David’s grave. The argument is explicit, though the psalm alone reads as rescue from death.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 16 predict resurrection? The psalm says God will not abandon His faithful one to the grave or let him see decay.
slides.body: The psalm says God will not abandon His faithful one to the grave or let him see decay.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 16 predict resurrection?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 16:10: You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
slides.body: You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
slides.heading: Ps 16:10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Acts 2:29–31, BSB: David died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day. But he was a prophet … Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ.
slides.body: David died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day. But he was a prophet … Foreseeing this, David spoke about the resurrection of the Christ.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Acts 2:29–31

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Acts makes the strongest possible case Two speeches quote it, contrast David’s grave with Jesus and apply it to his resurrection.
slides.body: Two speeches quote it, contrast David’s grave with Jesus and apply it to his resurrection.
slides.heading: Acts makes the strongest possible case

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the psalm itself describes rescue Its speaker trusts God to preserve his life. Dying and rising enter the passage through Acts’s later argument.
slides.body: Its speaker trusts God to preserve his life. Dying and rising enter the passage through Acts’s later argument.
slides.heading: But the psalm itself describes rescue

title: Your Holy One will not decay
